description:

title: 21st National Juried Exhibition
location: Axis Gallery, 625 S St, Sacramento, 95811, United States
description:
AXIS GALLERY
21st ANNUAL NATIONAL JURIED COMPETITION
August 7–30, 2026 
Second Saturday Reception August 8, 2026, 5–8 PM 
Axis Gallery presents the 21st Annual National Juried Competition, a group exhibition featuring works selected by juror Sharon Butler, founder of Two Coats of Paint. The exhibition includes works by artists from around the country in a variety of mediums. 
JUROR’S STATEMENT
The Axis Gallery received 658 submissions to an open call, and I could have selected five exhibitions instead of one without feeling professionally compromised. Narrowing such a high- quality profusion down to a single hang was a real challenge. Whereas traditional thematic trawls tend to be self-limiting, open calls like this one afford the juror no circumscribing guidance – only that of quality on the terms artists set for themselves. And the work I perused made it clear that artists throughout the country and across genres are richly engaged in conversations about ideas, materials, emotional content, and formal issues. The show’s density is testament to the abundance of pieces that were simply too good to leave out. 
Since no theme was handed down in advance, my job was to arrive at a selection piece by piece, submission by submission, until I saw the show take shape from what artists are concerned about and refracting through their work right now. I encountered a gnawing disquiet, an insistence on making things by hand, an interest in place, and the use of materiality and process as metaphor. Although I don’t believe most of the submitting artists know one another, the selected works seem connected, as if they might mutually complete sentences. And indeed, one virtue of an open call is that it is liable to produce an unplanned consensus – a kind of serendipity that might elude a more deliberately curated process with a long list of criteria. 
I’ll admit my own slight bias in the selection. I’m somewhat less interested in traditional technical skill than in inventiveness – in what happens when an artist reaches for something that isn’t supposed to be an art material at all, and in instances when artists find meaningful content in improbable subject matter. Some of the pieces here employ images or objects that may challenge the conventional view of what counts as art, and I kept coming back to those. This exhibition, then, represents one person’s path through a terrific field of entries. It is, I hope, a generous and thoughtful selection. I remain thoroughly impressed that when the Axis Gallery asked a wide, unfiltered public to submit work, the items that came in response were at once more surprising and more complementary than I had any right to expect. 
– Sharon Butler, July 2026 
ABOUT THE JUROR
Sharon Butler is a painter and the founder of Two Coats of Paint, an award-winning NYC blogazine about painting. She has held solo exhibitions in at CLEA RSKY, Jennifer Baahng Gallery, Theodore Gallery, Pocket Utopia, and Central Fine Arts (all in NYC); in Connecticut at Slater Memorial Museum, Real Art Ways, and Furnace Art on Paper Archive; and in the university galleries at University of Alabama, University of Connecticut, and SUNY Westchester. Her paintings are characterized by a tendency toward Casualism, a term she coined in an article published in The Brooklyn Rail to describe an approach to painting that values imperfection, incompleteness, and process over traditional color theory, pleasing composition, and polished forms.
Her work has been featured in publications such as The Brooklyn Rail, Hyperallergic, artcritical, The New Criterion, and New York Magazine. She has received awards from Creative Capital and the Warhol Foundation, Yaddo, Connecticut Commission on the Arts, and the Pollock-Krasner Foundation. 
She lives and works in Long Island City, Queens.

title: DMTC's Beginner's Improv Class
location: Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC), 607 Pena Dr.
description:
This beginner-friendly class introduces participants to the fundamentals of improv theatre in a fun, supportive, and low-pressure environment. Through ensemble activities, character exercises, and short-form improv games, participants will practice thinking on their feet, making bold creative choices, supporting their scene partners, and building confidence both on and off the stage. No previous improv or performance experience is required. Come ready to play, take creative risks, and discover what happens when you stop overthinking and say, “Yes, and!” 
Saturday, August 22 at 5:30PM-7:30PM 
Ages 18+ 
Instructor Information 
Chris Long has entertained audiences around the world for 30 years in more than 150 productions, including ballet, Shakespeare, musicals, and comedies. DMTC audiences may have recently seen him as Lord Farquaad in Shrek the Musical. Chris began teaching improv to high school students 20 years ago and continues to use improv training to help others strengthen their public-speaking skills, confidence, and quick thinking. 
Sofia Rosario has 20 years of theatre experience as a performer, stage manager, crew member, and arts administrator. A former member of her high school improv team, she later studied Musical Theatre at California State University, Fullerton. DMTC audiences may have seen her as Mrs. Lovett in Sweeney Todd or Vivienne Kensington in Legally Blonde.

location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change. 
  
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance. 
  
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.

title: Human Relations Commission Meetings
location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July). 
  
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site. 
  
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council. 
  
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org

title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

description:

This year is extra special as the Davis Farmers Market celebrates its 50th Anniversary! Don’t miss the big anniversary celebration on Saturday, August 1, 2026. 
New in 2026: The Market Memories Cookbook (presale now at davis-farmers-market). 
Highlights Include: 

Buckhorn Food Truck, The Hotdogger, Dhillon Farm, Davis Bread & Desserts, Greek Table, Kettle Pop & more
Live music every week
Kids’ activities
Local beer, wine & mead

Free to attend – everyone is welcome!

title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

title: Davis City Council Meetings
location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change. 
  
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance. 
  
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.

title: Human Relations Commission Meetings
location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July). 
  
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site. 
  
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council. 
  
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org

location: City Hall Community Chambers, 23 Russell Blvd, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July). 
  
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site. 
  
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council. 
  
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
